# The letters

After stating its system in brief, the 1446 book explained the letters one
class at a time: the initial consonants, the vowels, the final consonants.
Each class was explained by the same method.

This part does the same for gog's letters. The marks are the initial consonants:
visible forms that draw nothing until a position says where they go. The
positions are the vowels: `x`, `y`, and `z`, plus the scales that decide how a
number, a category, or a date becomes a place on an axis. The refining channels
are the finals: `color`, `size`, `shape`, `pattern`, `opacity`. Each is
optional, and each earns the legend that decodes it. `group` and `label` are
neither. `group` splits a mark without encoding anything, so it earns no legend,
and it works like the space between words. `label` supplies a `text` mark's
words rather than refining them. `play` stands outside the syllable, the way
faceting does: it cuts the plot into frames and plays them in order, and its
chapter waits in the next part. Around the letters sit the chapters that finish
a plot. [Data](../data.qmd), the table you bind once, opens this part, because
nothing can be drawn until a table is named. [The book's data](../book-data.qmd)
follows, saying where this book's own tables come from and how to read one in
your language. [Setting vs mapping](../style.qmd) separates a column you *map*
from a constant you *set*, and [Transforms](../transforms.qmd), which derives
new values from your columns, closes the part.

[Choosing a mark](../marks/index.qmd) opens the letters themselves, and then
each mark has a chapter of its own, fourteen in a row from
[point](../marks/point.qmd) to [edge](../marks/edge.qmd). Every one follows the
same template: what it draws, what it requires, what refines it, what derives
from it, what you can set on it, what it refuses, and what comes next. Those
three are always the last three, under those names, and thirteen of the fourteen
put a short summary of the mark's rules in front of them. That sameness is deliberate:
it is the [No Exceptions](../design-laws.qmd) law applied to a book's
structure. Learning the
second mark is faster than the first, and by the fifth you already know the
shape.
